diagnostics.message: `aws_cloudtrail.main` only references `aws_s3_bucket.cloudtrail` (via `s3_bucket_name`), so nothing in the graph forces `aws_s3_bucket_policy.cloudtrail` to be applied first. CloudTrail validates that it can write to the target bucket at creation time and fails with `InsufficientS3BucketPolicyException` if the trail bucket policy (AWSCloudTrailAclCheck / AWSCloudTrailWrite) is not already attached — an ordering gap that is worse on a fresh apply where the bucket is brand new. The provider's own example documents `depends_on = [aws_s3_bucket_policy.example]` on the trail for exactly this reason.

`module.eventbridge` creates rule targets that publish to `aws_sns_topic.security_alerts`, and therefore depends only on the topic itself. The topic's resource policy (`aws_sns_topic_policy.security_alerts`), which grants `events.amazonaws.com` `sns:Publish`, is established independently, so EventBridge can be created and begin matching rules before the topic accepts its publishes — matched CIS events are dropped with an authorization error. `module.eventbridge` should depend on `aws_sns_topic_policy.security_alerts` (and it should be destroyed before the policy).
